items.title: fuzz: add libFuzzer targets for OCI, protocol-state and volume-format parsers
items.body:
Refs #58. Based on main @ c86945b1, per the issue discussion.

Added (everything under fuzz/, 124 files, +849 lines; no root file modified):

fuzz/Cargo.toml — standalone cargo-fuzz workspace, not a root-workspace member; crates consumed via in-repo path deps (ginux-oci without default features + "sha256", ginux-protocol-state, ginux-volume-format); libfuzzer-sys = "=0.4.13"; committed fuzz/Cargo.lock (34 locked packages).
fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml — nightly-2026-11-02 + rust-src + llvm-tools-preview, scoped to fuzz/ (root 1.99.0/UEFI toolchain untouched).
Three targets with committed seeds + dictionaries: oci_surfaces (53 seeds; tar/PAX parse, published-rootfs traversal, registry/digest/bearer surfaces), protocol_surfaces (34; ARP/IPv4/ICMP parsers, neighbor state machine), volume_surfaces (26; kernel-faithful decode chain + encode). 113 seed files, 83.8 KB total; no evolved corpus, no crash artifacts.
fuzz/README.md — requirements, exact build/run commands, bounded smoke (~60 s per target), coverage how-to.
Latest run ([workflow run 41614443506](https://github.com/hafid-logic/ginux-watch/actions/runs/41614443506), branch sha eccb0de7): make doctor/check/architecture-check/test all 0/0/0/0 with fuzz/ present; documented smoke passes on all three targets; 10-minute rounds 24.9M / 101.6M / 46.3M execs (172.8M total), zero crashes, zero sanitizer reports; coverage (seeds + evolved corpus): regions 92.95/97.50/99.43%, functions 97.94/100/100%.

Not included: the differential PAX-vs-tar-crate harness — it adds the tar crate as an external dependency; can follow separately. No CI workflow added — upstream keeps its own minimal check.yml; README smoke reproduces anywhere.

New dependencies: libfuzzer-sys 0.4.13 (+ transitive deps, locked in fuzz/Cargo.lock). No other manifest is touched.

Draft; happy to split per target if review prefers. Analysis assisted by AI, reviewed by me. This adds fuzzing tooling; it is not a security claim.
